title: Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg · lung treatment component
context_label: First-line non-squamous NSCLC · platinum or EGFR/erlotinib context
therapy_label: Bevacizumab with a separately prescribed partner
schedule_summary: Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg is infused on Day 1 every 21 days. With platinum chemotherapy, the combined phase lasts up to six cycles, then bevacizumab may continue alone. With erlotinib, the combination continues while helpful and tolerated. Progression or unacceptable toxicity can stop either plan earlier; no fixed overall lung-treatment duration is promised.
purpose: Bevacizumab blocks VEGF, a signal that supports blood-vessel growth. In selected non-squamous lung cancers it is added to another treatment to help control cancer; the balance of benefit and risk depends on the partner and tumour features.
indication_text: NCCP 00215f: first-line unresectable advanced, recurrent or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with platinum-based chemotherapy. NCCP 00215g: the corresponding first-line EGFR-activating-mutation setting with erlotinib. This is the bevacizumab component; every partner needs its own prescription, assessment and consent.
administration_text: The usual bevacizumab reference dose is 15 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days. The first infusion is over 90 minutes; if tolerated, the second can be over 60 minutes and later infusions over 30 minutes. The team checks the actual prescription, blood pressure, urine and other tests before treatment.
monitoring_summary: Before starting: blood count, kidney and liver tests, urine protein, blood pressure and a heart history/examination. Repeat blood count, kidney/liver tests and urine testing before each cycle; check blood pressure before treatment and after it. Extra checks depend on symptoms and results.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Bevacizumab
agents.explanation: Binds VEGF, a signal that promotes blood-vessel growth. Blocking VEGF can reduce the blood supply that supports tumour growth; it also affects normal blood vessels and wound healing.
agents.mechanism: Blocks the VEGF blood-vessel growth signal
risks: Raised blood pressure and protein in the urine
Bleeding, blood clots and problems with wound healing
Rare bowel perforation, abnormal internal connections called fistulae, or serious wound infection
Rare severe headache, confusion, seizures or vision changes associated with a brain syndrome
Infusion reactions and fatigue; the partner treatment adds its own risks
agents.watch: Report bleeding, severe pain, neurological symptoms or wound problems promptly, and attend blood-pressure and urine checks.

anatomy: Severe headache, confusion, seizures or a change in vision need urgent help.
Attend blood-pressure checks; chest pain, breathlessness or a swollen painful leg need urgent help.
Urine checks look for protein. Report new swelling, foamy urine or reduced urine.
Sudden severe abdominal pain needs urgent assessment.
Report bleeding or wounds that are painful, red, spreading or slow to heal.
A new swollen painful leg or sudden breathlessness needs urgent help.
anatomy_note: Symptoms are prompts to contact the team, not a diagnosis. The selected partner has additional effects covered in its own guide.

monitoring_schedule.title: Treatment and checks

rows.label: Blood pressure
cells: More often if raised or symptomatic

rows.label: Heart / anticoagulation
cells: Heart history; ECHO if risk; INR if indicated
Warfarin INR before cycles once stable
INR weekly until stable; report symptoms

monitoring_schedule.note: These are relative planning stages, not booked appointments or equal time intervals. Extra blood-pressure, urine, heart or anticoagulation checks depend on individual risk and results.

urgent_extra: Seek urgent help for sudden severe abdominal pain, significant bleeding or coughing blood, chest pain, breathlessness, a swollen painful leg, a severe headache, confusion, seizures, a change in vision, or a rapidly painful/red spreading wound. Follow the chemotherapy emergency plan for fever or feeling acutely unwell.

sections.title: Infusion visits
sections.text: The usual bevacizumab reference dose is 15 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days. The first infusion is over 90 minutes; if tolerated, the second can be over 60 minutes and later infusions over 30 minutes. The team checks the actual prescription, blood pressure, urine and other tests before treatment.

sections.title: Checks and samples
sections.text: Allow time for blood tests, a urine sample and blood-pressure checks. A 24-hour urine collection may be needed between visits; confirm when the team needs the result.

sections.title: Partner treatment
sections.text: The platinum chemotherapy schedule or daily erlotinib plan is separate. Bring the complete written plan. After up to six platinum cycles, confirm whether bevacizumab alone continues; this phase change does not apply automatically to erlotinib.

sections.title: Access and procedures
sections.text: Bevacizumab needs an intravenous cannula or existing suitable central line; the team decides access. Tell the team about surgery, dental work or wounds before booking procedures.

sections.title: Support contacts
sections.text: Keep the daytime and out-of-hours oncology numbers available. If a visit or test is missed, contact the team for a revised plan rather than rearranging treatment yourself.

evidence.title: Evidence depends on the treatment partner
evidence.intro: Studies have tested bevacizumab with platinum chemotherapy and, separately, with erlotinib in cancers with certain EGFR mutations. The results answer different questions.
evidence.interpretation: Adding bevacizumab to carboplatin/paclitaxel improved survival in one historical trial. Adding it to erlotinib delayed progression in another trial without a demonstrated overall-survival improvement.
evidence.limitations: These findings concern complete combinations, not bevacizumab alone. They do not rank modern treatment options or predict an individual outcome.

teachback: Which lung pathway applies, when are bevacizumab and partner treatments due, when are blood-pressure and urine checks, and which symptoms need urgent help?
consent_support: Confirm the chosen lung pathway, disease-control aim, alternatives and the evidence for the specific partner. Discuss blood-pressure and urine monitoring, pulmonary and other bleeding, clots, bowel perforation/fistula, wound healing, infusion reactions, fertility/pregnancy precautions and all partner risks. The chemotherapy and erlotinib trials showed different outcomes; neither predicts an individual result.

support.title: Blood pressure and urine
support.text: Take prescribed blood-pressure medicines as agreed and attend urine checks. If a 24-hour collection is requested, confirm how to collect and return it before the next treatment.

support.title: Surgery, wounds and teeth
support.text: Tell the team about planned operations, dental procedures and any wound that is not healing. Bevacizumab can require a treatment break around procedures; the team sets the timing.

support.title: Separate partner support
support.text: Bevacizumab itself usually needs no routine anti-sickness premedication. Platinum chemotherapy needs its own anti-sickness and other support plan. Erlotinib needs its own tablet, interaction, skin and diarrhoea plan. Keep the complete plan and emergency numbers.

support.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
support.text: Discuss fertility and effective contraception before treatment and continue contraception during treatment and for at least six months after the last bevacizumab dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least six months after the final dose. The partner treatment may require additional precautions.

questions.q: Which lung pathway am I following?
questions.a: Ask whether you are receiving bevacizumab with platinum chemotherapy or with erlotinib for an EGFR-mutated cancer. Their partner schedules, checks and phase changes differ.

The platinum combination is given for up to six cycles, after which bevacizumab can continue alone if appropriate. The erlotinib pathway has no automatic six-cycle switch. The team reviews benefit, side effects and your priorities.

questions.q: What happens if urine protein or blood pressure rises?
questions.a: The team may repeat tests, treat blood pressure or pause bevacizumab. Severe problems may mean stopping it. Do not restart after a pause without an agreed plan.

questions.q: What if I need an operation or dental work?
questions.a: Tell the oncology team before the procedure. Bevacizumab can slow healing, and the team must coordinate any treatment break and check healing before restarting.

phases_note: Confirm the selected pathway. This guide covers bevacizumab only; the partner has its own full plan.

timeline.label: Symptoms / extra checks
timeline.text: Report early; follow the agreed BP and urine plan

timeline_note: One 21-day bevacizumab reference cycle without calendar dates. The selected partner follows its own schedule; the team reviews the next cycle and any phase change.
safety_note: Educational component reference. The treating team confirms the prescription and tests; the partner requires its own complete assessment and consent.

chronology_notes.title: Platinum pathway
chronology_notes.text: Bevacizumab every 21 days with the selected platinum chemotherapy for up to six cycles, followed by bevacizumab continuation while helpful and tolerated.

chronology_notes.title: EGFR/erlotinib pathway
chronology_notes.text: Bevacizumab every 21 days alongside separately prescribed daily erlotinib while helpful and tolerated; no automatic six-cycle switch.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment pauses
chronology_notes.text: Surgery, wound healing, bleeding, blood pressure, urine protein or other problems may change the plan. The team confirms when or whether to restart.

items.title: Urine results
items.text: Protein in the urine can require a 24-hour collection and additional checks. Your team explains how and when to collect it, and reviews whether treatment can continue.

items.title: Heart and blood-thinning medicines
items.text: An ultrasound of the heart may be considered if you have had certain earlier chemotherapy or chest-wall radiotherapy. If you take warfarin, INR tests are usually weekly until stable and then before each cycle; follow your individual plan.

items.title: Cancer response
items.text: Scans and cancer-response checks follow the individual consultant plan. This guide does not promise a fixed scan or repeat heart-ultrasound schedule.
